scientific_question: Does a single path-integrated 2MRS foreground-density score explain Pantheon+ Hubble residual structure beyond a fixed-axis dipole and nuisance controls?
smoothing_provenance: carried forward from the strongest controlled regression smoothing in the March 2026 exploratory 2MRS scan; not rescanned in this test
foreground_rule: Only the fraction of a galaxy shell lying in front of each SN contributes.
shell_density_definition: Gaussian-smoothed 2MRS count at the SN direction, standardized within each shell across the SN sightline sample.
score_normalization: z-score F_raw over the analysis sample; normalization uses no SN residual information
primary_model: Hubble residual ~ intercept + foreground_score + fixed_axis_cosine + available host-mass and survey controls
null_model: Hubble residual ~ intercept + fixed_axis_cosine + same nuisance controls

permutation.type: shuffle foreground score within fixed SN-redshift blocks
permutation.two_sided_sign_policy: source-export sign remains open; significance is based on Delta chi2

classification.strong: blocked permutation p < 0.01 AND foreground coefficient sign is stable under all leave-one-shell-out checks

secondary_transfer_test.rule: fit one foreground amplitude at low z, carry it unchanged to the higher-z sample, and report weighted residual improvement without refitting the foreground amplitude

claim_boundary: 2MRS galaxy density is a foreground-structure proxy, not yet a BHSM-specific de-encapsulation map
ordinary peculiar-velocity, lensing, selection and density effects remain possible explanations
no shell-specific foreground coefficient may be selected after seeing the residuals
no current-data smoothing optimization is allowed
